# Analysis 6: Regional Decisions

## Decision

Use shared measurement and reversible tests, then prioritize regional diagnostics.
The original JP-only launch-warning claim is withdrawn after the payer audit:
all regions breach both launch and post-14 adjacent-offer guardrails. No composite
score combines revenue, retention points and participation indices.

| region | fantasy_d30_change_pp | astra_d30_change_pp | astra_normal_participation_index | bm_launch_revenue_change_pct | bm_adjacent_launch_change_pct | bm_adjacent_post_14_change_pct | incident_nru_recovery_index | incident_d30_change_pp |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KR | 2.37 | -2.40 | 81.57 | 59.78 | -10.63 | -12.64 | 86.20 | -0.67 |
| JP | 3.79 | -2.13 | 81.29 | 57.70 | -7.55 | -10.83 | 106.55 | -1.02 |

KR has the lowest NRU recovery index, so acquisition mix is an investigation
priority; channel causes and CAC are unobserved. JP retains the strongest Fantasy
D30 improvement, but no longer has a unique offer-warning mechanism. Global West
combines the strongest launch-revenue response with the largest launch adjacency
and post-recovery D30 gaps; additional spend should await quality diagnostics.

Equality semantics match source analyses: D30 at -1 pp and adjacency at -5%
are warnings; entry at 90 and residual D30 at -0.5 pp pass. Five checks warn in
all regions under the published payer assumption; daily operational exits pass.
These authored thresholds are not industry standards or statistical significance.

## Actions

| scope | priority | theme | action | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ALL | P0-1 | Test entry hypothesis | Instrument exposure, eligibility and first attempt before selecting an entry treatment. | Low aggregate boss participation coexists with weak D30; individual paths are unobserved. |
| ALL | P0-2 | Recurring-offer diagnostic | Audit payer overlap, then test differentiated benefits with a holdout. | Launch adjacent change ranges from -14.57% to -7.55%; inspect payer assumptions before causal claims. |
| ALL | P0-3 | Recovery exit criteria | Track activity, commercial and mature-cohort recovery separately. | Daily operational checks and D30 checks use different populations and horizons. |
| KR | P1 | Acquisition and entry diagnosis | Inspect acquisition mix and eligibility before scaling spend or changing difficulty. | NRU recovery index 86.20; Astra entry index 81.57; D30 change -2.40 pp. |
| KR | P2 | Offer and recovery quality | Test catalog differentiation; retain mature-cohort monitoring after operational recovery. | Launch adjacency -10.63%; post-14 -12.64%; residual D30 -0.67 pp. |
| JP | P1 | Acquisition and entry diagnosis | Inspect acquisition mix and eligibility before scaling spend or changing difficulty. | NRU recovery index 106.55; Astra entry index 81.29; D30 change -2.13 pp. |
| JP | P2 | Offer and recovery quality | Test catalog differentiation; retain mature-cohort monitoring after operational recovery. | Launch adjacency -7.55%; post-14 -10.83%; residual D30 -1.02 pp. |
| GLOBAL_WEST | P1 | Acquisition and entry diagnosis | Inspect acquisition mix and eligibility before scaling spend or changing difficulty. | NRU recovery index 98.53; Astra entry index 82.97; D30 change -2.58 pp. |
| GLOBAL_WEST | P2 | Offer and recovery quality | Test catalog differentiation; retain mature-cohort monitoring after operational recovery. | Launch adjacency -14.57%; post-14 -15.43%; residual D30 -1.58 pp. |

Low boss entry plus normal participant outcomes supports an entry hypothesis;
it does not locate individual dropout or rule out power-based selection.
Likewise, service-cohort D30 does not trace incident survivors. Follow the
[decision plan](../decision_plan.md), including telemetry, experimental unit,
primary outcome, guardrails and the decision that would change.
